q: Does fly ash from a coal power plant carry any of the plant's emissions?
title: Fly ash: does it carry plant emissions?
short: Usually almost none. Many product footprint rules and EPD programmes treat fly ash as a waste or a low value by product, so only its collection, drying, grinding and transport are counted. Some use economic allocation, which adds a small share, so ask what rule a cement or brick supplier used.
audience: Cement, brick and block makers buying fly ash from Korba and other thermal plants, and their buyers

ul: Fly ash as waste: zero share of combustion emissions, only handling and transport counted.
Fly ash as co product: a share by economic value, small because ash sells cheaply.
Never by mass, which would load most of the plant's CO2 onto ash.

p: Trucking or rail from the plant to your site, any drying, and grinding power. These are real and often larger than people expect over long distances.
Fly ash lowers clinker or clay use, so blended cement and fly ash bricks often show lower figures. Make sure the supplier's rule is stated so the comparison is fair.
